section_summary: This section begins with the end of a compilation of Japanese broadcasts about transport, finance, agriculture, and administration in Japanese-occupied territories. It then contains U.S. Embassy telegrams and despatches forwarding monitored broadcasts, a translation of former envoy Kurusu’s November 1942 speech, and an extensive report on Premier Tojo’s January 1943 Diet speech. Later documents discuss a Japan–Bulgaria convention, distribution of broadcast reports, and an Embassy assessment that Japanese broadcasts had become less confident by March 1943.

subfiles.title: Compilation of Japanese broadcast summaries on occupied Asia
subfiles.about: Japanese broadcasts report economic, transport, agricultural, financial, and administrative measures across Japan and occupied Asia.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages of a numbered compilation describe bus, rail, postal, telegraph, banking, and shipping developments; savings campaigns; rice and other crop production; and resource development. They also report financial and trade policies in Malaya, Sumatra, Indochina, China, Borneo, and the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1114: summaries of Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Soviet-monitored Japanese broadcast summaries on production, trade, transport, and resources.
subfiles.summary: Three sections summarize broadcasts from late November and early December 1942. Subjects include Japanese and Manchukuo crops, industrial output, taxes, postal links, Thailand relations, and Sakhalin transport, followed by claims about Java’s agricultural and mineral wealth.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 1114, first section
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The paraphrase summarizes broadcasts on Japanese harvests, industrial production, and Hong Kong postal service.
subfiles.summary: Tojo calls for greater peasant effort despite improved crops; other broadcasts discuss Hokkaido coal, Central China minerals, and restored Hong Kong postal links.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 1114, remaining sections
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The paraphrase covers an East Asian economic conference and broadcasts about Manchukuo and Java.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasts report an East Asian economic conference, Manchurian agriculture and mining, Japan–Thailand ties, and new postal and rail links. They claim that Manchukuo’s production and savings are strong and give output figures for Java’s rice, sugar, rubber, tobacco, cinchona, and minerals.

subfiles.title: Despatch 147 transmitting monitored broadcasts
subfiles.from: Charles E. Dickerson, Jr., American Embassy, Kuibyshev
subfiles.about: The Embassy transmits Russian texts of Japanese broadcasts summarized in an earlier telegram.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Soviet-monitored broadcast texts cited in Moscow telegram 430.

subfiles.title: Despatch 129 transmitting monitored broadcasts
subfiles.from: Charles E. Dickerson, Jr., American Embassy, Kuibyshev
subfiles.about: The Embassy transmits Russian texts of broadcasts monitored from September 18 to October 11.
subfiles.summary: Forwards full Russian texts of Japanese broadcasts previously summarized by telegram.

subfiles.title: Transmission of broadcast despatches to FCC
subfiles.about: The State Department sends two Embassy despatches and their broadcast enclosures to the FCC.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Kuibyshev despatches 129 and 147 with Soviet-monitored Japanese broadcast texts.

subfiles.title: Comparison of Kurusu speech translations
subfiles.about: A State Department file note compares translations of Kurusu’s November 26 speech.
subfiles.summary: Finds the Chinese-source and FCC-monitored translations substantially alike.

subfiles.title: Despatch 778 transmitting Kurusu speech
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: The Embassy encloses a translation of Kurusu’s radio speech from a Chinese text.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the requested translation obtained through Quo Tai-chi.

subfiles.title: Translation of former envoy Kurusu’s November 26 speech
subfiles.about: Kurusu presents a Japanese account of the failed 1941 negotiations with the United States and the origins of war.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu portrays the November 26, 1941 U.S. proposal as an ultimatum and assigns responsibility for war to the United States. He recounts embargoes, the freezing of Japanese assets, and the Washington negotiations, then attacks Allied war aims and urges Japan to continue fighting. The text is a translation of a wartime broadcast and presents Kurusu’s claims.

subfiles.title: Telegram 26: Japanese broadcast summaries
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes December broadcasts on food, oil, shipping, transport, and industrial supply.
subfiles.summary: The broadcasts claim increased Borneo oil and coal output, operating Hong Kong shipyards, and improved Japanese access to Dutch East Indies petroleum. They also describe food conservation campaigns, a Sumatra railway, renamed Batavia, Chinese roads, petroleum trading controls, and clothing distribution in Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 26
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates the Embassy’s December Japanese broadcast summaries.
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese claims about Borneo resources, Hong Kong shipbuilding, food conservation, Sumatra and Chinese transport, oil supplies, war contributions, petroleum regulation, and Manchukuo clothing production.

subfiles.title: Despatch 194 transmitting monitored broadcasts
subfiles.from: Loy W. Henderson, American Embassy, Kuibyshev
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Russian texts of Japanese broadcasts cited in Moscow telegram 514.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Soviet-monitored texts previously summarized by telegram.

subfiles.title: Despatch 196 transmitting monitored broadcasts
subfiles.from: Charles E. Dickerson, Jr., American Embassy, Kuibyshev
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Russian texts corresponding to telegram 1114.
subfiles.summary: Transmits full Soviet-monitored texts of broadcasts summarized on December 18.

subfiles.title: Despatch 225 transmitting monitored broadcasts
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, American Embassy, Kuibyshev
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Russian broadcast texts corresponding to telegram 26.
subfiles.summary: Transmits texts of Japanese broadcasts summarized in the January 6 telegram.

subfiles.title: FBIS supplement on Premier Tojo’s Diet speech
subfiles.about: The report reproduces English broadcast coverage and translated excerpts of Tojo’s January 27 Diet speech.
subfiles.summary: Tojo claims Japan has secured strategic positions and vital resources, calls 1943 a year of decisive battles, and promises continued offensives against the United States and Britain. He discusses cooperation with Manchukuo, Thailand, Germany, Italy, and the Nanking government, as well as prospective Burmese and Philippine independence. Additional translated excerpts address occupied territories, India, the Japanese home front, production, and war mobilization.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Japan–Bulgaria convention
subfiles.about: The memorandum assesses a broadcast announcement of a Japan–Bulgaria cultural convention.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes its amity and cultural provisions and calls it a political gesture.

subfiles.title: Tokyo broadcast of Japan–Bulgaria convention
subfiles.about: The broadcast announces and reproduces the Japan–Bulgaria Convention of Amity and Cultural Collaboration.
subfiles.summary: Gives the signatories and three articles on amity, cultural cooperation, and duration.

subfiles.title: FCC memorandum requesting diplomatic-pouch distribution
subfiles.from: Harold N. Graves, Jr., Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service
subfiles.about: The FCC asks that its Radio Report on the Far East be sent regularly to London.
subfiles.summary: Requests diplomatic-pouch delivery of current and future reports to British ministries.
keywords: Radio Report on the Far East

subfiles.title: FCC letter on Radio Report distribution
subfiles.from: Robert D. Leigh, Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service
subfiles.about: The FBIS adds the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to its regular report distribution.
subfiles.summary: Confirms regular delivery of the Radio Report on the Far East and back issues.
keywords: Radio Report on the Far East

subfiles.title: Telegram 129 on the changing tone of Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.about: The Embassy observes less confidence and more discussion of shortages in Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasts since the start of 1943 show diminished triumphalism and more emphasis on supply, raw materials, food, labor, and sacrifice.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 129
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates the Embassy’s assessment of a changed broadcast tone.
subfiles.summary: Notes reduced confidence and repeated appeals for production and sacrifice.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to Chungking on Japanese broadcast tone
subfiles.about: The Department analyzes Japanese broadcasts about shortages, shipping, and wartime restrictions.
subfiles.summary: A survey finds fewer claims of victory and more discussion of agricultural, material, and shipping difficulties. It cites a January 18 German-language broadcast on restrictions and suggests possible propaganda purposes for the changed tone.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese broadcasts, section one
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes late December broadcasts on Manchukuo, the Philippines, transport, and savings.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasts describe a Manchukuo horse-breeding project and production appeals; railway restoration and 1943 administrative plans in the Philippines; fortifications in the Gilbert Islands; planned Manchukuo roads and railways; Japanese savings; reduced household gas supply; and Tojo’s appeal for more farm output.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese broadcasts, section two
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes broadcasts on banks, agriculture, cotton, health, and rubber regulation.
subfiles.summary: Reports new banking and school activity in Manila, Manchukuo development and youth labor service, agricultural expansion in Timor, and Japanese appeals for zinc production. Further items concern opium enforcement, Philippine cotton and sanitation, rubber purchasing controls, and plague-control training.
